import html # Pre‑defined template for user profiles. # The placeholders are :name:, :bio: and :status:. PROFILE_FORMAT = ( "
\n" "

{name}

\n" "

{bio}

\n" "

Status: {status}

\n" "
" ) def create_user_profile(user_name: str, biography: str, status: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized and formatted user profile string. Parameters ---------- user_name : str The user's full name. biography : str A multi‑sentence biography provided by the user. status : str A brief, current status update from the user. Returns ------- str The sanitized and formatted HTML profile snippet. Raises ------ ValueError If any argument is not a string or is empty. """ # Basic type and emptiness checks for arg_name, value in (("user_name", user_name), ("biography", biography), ("status", status)): if not isinstance(value, str): raise ValueError(f"{arg_name} must be a string") if not value.strip(): raise ValueError(f"{arg_name} cannot be empty or whitespace") # Escape user input to neutralize XSS attacks. safe_name = html.escape(user_name, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(biography, quote=True) safe_status = html.escape(status, quote=True) # Format the profile using the predefined template. formatted_profile = PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status=safe_status ) return formatted_profile
